name: Question 13
problem: Consider the straight line that passes through $P(3,-2,3)$ and is parallel to $v=⟨-2,1,2⟩.$ Find all the possible points $A$ on that line such that $AP=3.$
worked_solution:
First, we find the vector equation of the line, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =⟨3,-2,3⟩+t⟨-2,1,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

Since $A$ lies on the line, we know that there must be a real number $t$ such that

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{OA} & =⟨3,-2,3⟩+t⟨-2,1,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PA} & =\overset{\to }{OA}-\overset{\to }{OP} \\  & =(⟨3,-2,3⟩+t⟨-2,1,2⟩)-⟨3,-2,3⟩ \\  & =t\,⟨-2,1,2⟩ \\  & =⟨-2t,\,t,\,2t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the fact that $PA=3,$ we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}AP & =3 \\ |\overset{\to }{PA}| & =3 \\ |⟨-2t,\,t,\,2t⟩| & =3 \\ \sqrt{(-2t)^{2}+{t}^{2}+(2t)^{2}} & =3 \\ \sqrt{4{t}^{2}+{t}^{2}+4{t}^{2}} & =3 \\ \sqrt{9{t}^{2}} & =3 \\ \pm 3t & =3 \\ t & =\pm 1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, putting the values $t=\pm 1$ into the equation for the line, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \overset{\to }{O{A}_{1}}=⟨3,-2,3⟩+⟨-2,1,2⟩=⟨1,-1,5⟩, \\  & \overset{\to }{O{A}_{2}}=⟨3,-2,3⟩-⟨-2,1,2⟩=⟨5,-3,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the points are ${A}_{1}(1,-1,5)$ and ${A}_{2}(5,-3,1).$

Question 13
?

Consider the straight line that passes through P(3,−2,3) and is parallel to v=⟨−2,1,2⟩. Find all the possible points A on that line such that AP=3.

a
A1(1,−1,5) and A2(5,−3,1)
b
A1(1,2,5) and A2(−5,3,1)
c
A1(1,1,−5) and A2(5,3,2)
d
A1(1,−1,−5) and A2(5,3,2)
e
A1(−1,−1,5) and A2(4,−3,−1)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we find the vector equation of the line, as follows:

r=p+tvr=⟨3,−2,3⟩+t⟨−2,1,2⟩ where t∈(−∞,∞).

Since A lies on the line, we know that there must be a real number t such that

OA→=⟨3,−2,3⟩+t⟨−2,1,2⟩

and

PA→=OA→−OP→=(⟨3,−2,3⟩+t⟨−2,1,2⟩)−⟨3,−2,3⟩=t⟨−2,1,2⟩=⟨−2t,t,2t⟩.

Using the fact that PA=3, we get:

AP=3|PA→|=3|⟨−2t,t,2t⟩|=3(−2t)2+t2+(2t)2=34t2+t2+4t2=39t2=3±3t=3t=±1

Finally, putting the values t=±1 into the equation for the line, we obtain

OA1→=⟨3,−2,3⟩+⟨−2,1,2⟩=⟨1,−1,5⟩,OA2→=⟨3,−2,3⟩−⟨−2,1,2⟩=⟨5,−3,1⟩. Therefore, the points are A1(1,−1,5) and A2(5,−3,1).
